title: archkeel core frame, protocol archkeel-core-frame-1
description: The one frame that the core writes and the shell reads. Generated from the types that write it.

rules.description: The kind word and the verdict of each decided rule.

explained.description: The reason of each UNKNOWN rule.

violations.description: The number of violations of each FAIL rule.

beyond.description:
Each PASS rule of a run with kept pair gaps: the reference engine gives it UNKNOWN, and
the model proves that no kept gap can change it (AD-384 point 4).

scope.description: Why the scope of the run is not complete, or `complete`.

premise.description:
The one assumption that the collector states for its proofs (AD-540). The word of `scope`
stays `complete`: the shell reads it.

gaps.description: The gaps of the rules without a decision, each with its kind (AD-546).

system.description: The parts of a system run (AD-616); `crate::system::join` writes it.

anyOf.description: One reason for each rule, by rule id.

RuleReasons.description: The reasons of the rules without a decision: one for each rule, or one for the contract.

oneOf.description: Every rule passes.
At least one rule fails.
At least one rule is unknown and none fails.

Status.description: The status of a run or of its observation: the three verdicts of the Decision.

oneOf.description: The rule holds.
The rule is broken.
The facts do not decide the rule.
The rule only declares and has no verdict.

RuleVerdict.description:
The encoded verdict of one rule row. It is the wire form only: a built report writes it from
a `Decision` of the model, and a decoded report holds it as read bytes (AD-363 point 4).

oneOf.description: The scope of the run is not complete.
No receipt proves the pass.
Some assessments are not decided.
A module with no owner blocks the rule.
No rule of the kind decides.

WhyUnknown.description:
Why the evaluator left a rule UNKNOWN. The builder derives the reason of every other verdict
from the `Decision`: PASS is `evaluated`, FAIL `violations`, a declaration `declaration`.

source.description: The id of the part that uses the interface.

target.description: The id of the part that provides it.

schema.description: The repository path of the schema of what crosses.

InterfaceRow.description: One interface between two parts of a system frame: a crossing that is no import.

calls_total.description: All calls that the inventory found.

calls_partial.description: Calls with a target that is only partly proven.

calls_external.description: Calls of a name outside the scan.

unresolved_name.description: Unresolved calls of a plain name.

unresolved_dynamic.description: Unresolved calls whose target is computed at run time.

typing_positions.description: The positions that a type annotation can fill.

untyped_private_accesses.description: Accesses to a private member that no type proves.

Measures.description: The counts of one complete source inventory.

requires.description: The declared structure (AD-594): each `requires` entry and each `layer_order`.

layer.description: The declared layer and the declared public surface. Empty when the contract states none.

responsibilities.description: What the component is responsible for, as the contract states it.

forbidden_responsibilities.description: What the component must not do, as the contract states it.

planned_public.description: The selectors of its planned surface. Empty when the contract states none.

language.description: The language of the collector reply that names the module.

imports.description: Zero says that no observed import uses the permission.

rationale.description: Why the contract allows the pair.

through.description: The selectors that an import of the pair must pass through; empty when the entry names none.

Require.description: One `requires` entry: the two components by id, and the observed imports that use it.

part.description: The component id of the owning system part, absent for a single project.

LayerOrder.description: The layers of one `layer_order` rule, from the inner layer to the outer layer.

index.description: The position of the violation in `details` of the rule.

CyclePath.description: One cycle: its members and one closed path through them.

Step.description: One step of a cycle path.

gaps_total.description: The number of coverage gaps of the reply.

gaps_holding.description: The number of coverage gaps that hold at least one rule.

gaps.description: The ids of the coverage gaps of the reply that hold the rule.

pairs.description: The pairs of the gaps between two modules that hold the rule.

total.description: The number of gaps that hold the rule.

unnamed_imports.description: The imports that the collector could not resolve and that no gap names.

RuleHolds.description: The gaps that hold one rule.

oneOf.description: Any other cause: the text of `explained` names it.

HoldKind.description: What kind of gap holds a rule.

Pair.description: The pair of a gap between two modules.

GapHolds.description: One coverage gap and the rules that it holds.

SectionRow.description: One row of a section: the envelope and the typed body (`kind` and `data`).

EvidenceClass.description: Whether the row states a fact of the code or a violation of a rule.

Area.description: The area of the picture that a row belongs to.

ConstructData.description: A forbidden construct: with the selector of the rule, or the plain construct name.

Collect.description:
The `collect` part of the self-test of a scan (AD-406): the request that the core derived and
the digest of each contract file, or the reason that the collector did not run.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version that the reply must use.

snapshot.description: The tree that the collector reads.

scope.description: The files that the collector reads.

resolver.description: The resolver settings of the language.

Request.description:
One collection request. `R` is the settings of the language: the whole `Resolver` as the wire
has it, or the settings of one language after the collector has chosen it.

oneOf.description: Protocol 3, the oldest request.
Protocol 8.
Protocol 9: the scope can exclude test sources.
Protocol 10: the request of the native Python collector.

Version.description: A request version that the host sends to a native collector.

git_head.description: The commit that the tree is at.

dirty.description: `true`, `false` or `"unknown"`, echoed back in the reply.

anyOf.description: Whether the tree has uncommitted changes.

Dirty.description: `dirty` is a Boolean, or the text `unknown` when the host could not read the work tree.

oneOf.description: The tool could not tell whether the tree is dirty.

UnknownDirty.description: The value of `dirty` when the tool cannot tell.

roots.description: Nonempty relative paths that stay inside the snapshot and neither repeat nor overlap.

Scope.description: The part of the snapshot to read.

tsconfig.description: A relative path that stays inside the snapshot.

bundler.description: The host writes `bundler` only when it is true, so false has one form: absent.

oneOf.description: The settings of the TypeScript resolver.
The settings of the Rust resolver.

phase.description: The phase of the Python collection.

interpreter.description: The interpreter that the collector runs.

oneOf.description: The settings of the Python resolver.
The settings of the Dart resolver.

Resolver.description: The settings of one language. The tag is the language that the collector reads.

oneOf.description: The import survey.

PythonPhase.description: The part of the Python collection that the request asks for. Slice 1 has the import survey.

version.description: `platform.python_version()`, for example `3.11.12`: the version that the facts claim.

builtin_module_names.description: `sys.builtin_module_names`, sorted. The set depends on the build, not on the version.

Interpreter.description:
What the host interpreter is, as one isolated child (`python -I`) sees it. The host builds it
in one function (`analyzer/interpreter.py`); the collector reads it and never runs Python.

detail.description: The collector's free text beside the reason, not part of the gap key (AD-540).

GapRow.description: One gap of the result, with the word that the shell reads (AD-546).

accepted_entries.description: The distinct entries (kind, subject, reason) that the file and the run share.

accepted_unknowns.description: The items behind them: an entry with a count of 3 is 3 items.

accepted_rules.description:
The rule rows whose every key the file accepts. The row stays UNKNOWN; the report says
"accepted" beside it.

Part.description: The part of the frame. `file` holds the bytes to write, as text.

Difference.description: One difference between the run and the file.

Named.description: A part of the baseline that the core names and does not decide.

document.description: The repository path of the system document.

parts.description: Each part, in the order of the document.

interfaces.description: What crosses between the parts, in the order of the document.

SystemFrame.description: The part `system` of a frame (AD-616): `crate::system::join` writes it.

config.description: The repository path of the configuration of the part.

profile.description: The profile of the collector that read the part, from its collection request.

rules.description: The ids of the rules of the part.

PartRow.description: One part of a system frame.
